declarations.docstring: Evaluating the first general-linear representation translates the evaluation argument by left division.
Evaluating the matrix polynomial transform agrees with evaluating the original polynomial after multiplication by the transposed matrix.
A monoid homomorphism from a general linear group to itself.
A self-map of the general linear group.
The underlying matrix of this map is the transpose of the inverse matrix.
The monoid homomorphism acts by transposing the inverse matrix.
Matrix evaluation at an invertible matrix sends every element of the indicated powers submonoid to a unit.
The matrix polynomial map sends the localized polynomial to its determinant scalar multiple.
An algebra homomorphism from a multivariable polynomial algebra to a localization, parametrized by a matrix.
This homomorphism factors matrix polynomial evaluation through the canonical localization map.
A representation of a product of two general linear groups on a localization.
The product representation applies the first and second factor endomorphisms in succession.
A general-linear-indexed algebra endomorphism of the localization.
On polynomial images in the localization, the first action is given by evaluation at the transformed invertible matrix.
The first action commutes with the companion algebra endomorphism.
The first action takes group multiplication to composition of algebra endomorphisms.
The first action at the identity is the identity algebra homomorphism.
A representation of the general linear group on the localization.
On polynomial images in the localization, the representation is determined by a transformed matrix evaluation.
The representation and the first action give the same endomorphism on every localization element.
The two indicated representations commute.
Builds a representation of a direct-product monoid from two pointwise commuting representations.
The direct-product representation acts by applying the second representation and then the first.
